segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: This juncture, the Chair would like to read this opening statement to our esteemed colleague, Senator Lacson, guests and resource persons, and the Department of Economy Planning and Development and its attached agencies.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We are here today to deliberate the proposed fiscal year 2027.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: The budget of the Department of Economy Planning and Development, attached agencies, and corporation.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: As we have emphasized during the DBCC briefing, our fiscal space is limited.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Kaya kailangan talagang piliin natin, nating mabuti kung saan mapupunta ang bawat piso ng ating budget.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: This becomes even more important given the economic challenges confronting our country.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We continue to feel the effects of external shocks,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: at iba pang mga pangunahing pangangailangan.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We are living at a time when the peso is at its slowest,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: while inflation rates are on the rise.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Our economy grew by only 4.4% in 2025,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: and growth has remained weak this year.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: and while the poverty rate has declined,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Filipinos are still living below the poverty line.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: These numbers should remind us that economic growth cannot be measured by statistics alone.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Ang tunay na sukatan ay kung gumaan ba ang buhay ng ating makababayan.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: This is where DEP-DEB plays an important role.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: You help determine where our country is going,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: and which programs and infrastructure projects will produce the greatest and most lasting benefit

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: DepDEP will also be the primary government agency to oversee and ensure the fulfillment of the promises of the Master Plan for Infrastructure and National Development, or the MIND Act, once it becomes a law.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: I'm very hopeful that whatever budget given to DepDEP will aid them in preparing for the implementation of the MIND Act.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: As we go through the budget, we want to know whether the resources being proposed for 2027 will allow DepDEP to fully perform its role in shaping our country's development, guiding government priorities, and helping improve the lives of our people.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: At the end of the day, the question is simple. Will this budget help DepDEP do its part in creating more jobs, reducing poverty, raising incomes, strengthening our economy, and giving Filipino families a better quality of life?

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We hope that by the end of today's presentation and deliberations, the answer to that question will be a clear yes. Thank you very much.

segments.text: Kaya ginagamit nila ang ating national ID system for authentication. Either facial recognition or di kaya yung fingerprint. So we feel, although mayroon tayong delay per timetable, one, because of the COVID, medyo nahihirapan tayo din sa COVID.

segments.speaker: PSA Undersecretary Claire Dennis S. Mapa
segments.text: But right now, ang ating projection sa authentication versus registration, kasi sa mga national ID ng ibang bansa, tinitingnan nila ilan ba yung nag-authenticate versus nag-register.

segments.speaker: PSA Undersecretary Claire Dennis S. Mapa
segments.text: So ang ating projection ngayong taon, mga nasa 1.5 times na-registered. So that would be about 150 million. But as we progress, aabot tayo dapat sa mga 4 to 5 authentications per registered person.

segments.speaker: PSA Undersecretary Claire Dennis S. Mapa
segments.text: So dapat mga nasa 4 million to 5 million per year. Yun po yung datos ngayon, Mr. Chair, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: PSA Undersecretary Claire Dennis S. Mapa
segments.text: On the question sa late registration, I agree sa observation. Ang registration kasi sa birth certificate, una, it's a universal right. Everybody, Pilipinos, must be registered.

segments.speaker: PSA Undersecretary Claire Dennis S. Mapa
segments.text: That's why the Philippine Statistics Authority is really putting program for the registration. Right now, Your Honor, ang ating registered persons, mga 97% of the total population.

segments.speaker: PSA Undersecretary Claire Dennis S. Mapa
segments.text: So mayroon pa tayong mga 3% na hindi pa na-register. So multiply again by about 114 million, so mga 3.5 million pa ang hindi re-registrado. Substantial number ay nasa BARM.

segments.speaker: PSA Undersecretary Claire Dennis S. Mapa
segments.text: About half of the registered sa BARM.

segments.speaker: PSA Undersecretary Claire Dennis S. Mapa
segments.text: Now, ito rin po, dahil may late registration tayo, hindi kasi natin pwedeng itigil yung late registration kasi kawawa naman yung mga Pilipino na wala silang birth certificate. But of course, may problem tayo na yung mga non-Filipinos that are registered.

segments.speaker: Senator Raffy T. Tulfo
segments.text: Mr. Chair, with the indulgence of [unclear], can I interject?

segments.speaker: Senator Raffy T. Tulfo
segments.text: Sa late registration, kasi matagal na itong pinag-usapan ni Park sa mga previous hearings, I raised this question.

segments.speaker: Senator Raffy T. Tulfo
segments.text: Yung sa late registration, where will it end?

segments.speaker: Senator Raffy T. Tulfo
segments.text: Sabi mo, walang katapusan ito. Dapat meron. Dapat darating yung time na wala ng late registration. Sa ngayon kasi, ang tanong ko, so paano yung compliance sa personal appearance, paano nyo po in-implement sa late registration?

segments.text: So we issued a memo that if you are a late registrant sa birth certificate,
